data.title: Dolné Vestenice – a drawing of the Slavic hillfort
data.excerpt: Tomáš Humaj has drawn his idea of how the Slavic hillfort at Dolné Vestenice looked – a site discovered only a few years ago, which has yielded a large number of beautiful finds from the period of Great Moravia. Because it stands on what is literally a table mountain, a wooden palisade was enough along most of its circuit and a massive rampart was built only on the more accessible northern side.

mediaTexts.alt: A pen drawing of an elongated hillfort with a palisade, a gateway and houses along the ridge

children.text: Tomáš Humaj has given us a fine Christmas present – he has drawn his idea of how the

looked, a site that was discovered only a few years ago and has been published only now. A large number of beautiful finds from the period of Great Moravia have been made at this hillfort. In the rock below the hillfort there is an overhang in which the remains of a smithy were found. The hillfort stands on what is literally a table mountain, so there was no need to build massive rampart defences here and along most of its circuit a wooden palisade was sufficient. Only in the northern part, where access was easier, was a massive rampart built. The entrance gateway was probably there as well. I warmly recommend a visit to this exceptional place to everyone...
